title: The Saviour, What a Noble Flame
description: The Saviour, What a Noble Flame in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: William Cowper wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 223 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “"He steadfastly set his face to go to Jerusalem."”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The Sa-viour, what a no-ble flame, Was kin-dled in his breast, When hast-ing to Je-ru-sa-lem, He marched be-fore the rest!

lines: The Saviour, what a noble flame,
Good-will to men, and zeal for God,
He goes to be baptized with blood;
He goes to meet the cross.
With all his sufferings full in view,
Forth to the task his spirit flew;
And while his holy sorrows here
We learn our lighter cross to bear,

licence: Public domain: William Cowper died in 1800.
credits: Words by William Cowper (1731–1800), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
